For the reaction 2A B + C, KC = 4 × 10–3. At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is: [A]
= [B] = [C] = 2 × 10–3 M. Then, which of the following is correct?
(1)
Reaction is at equilibrium.
(2)
Reaction has a tendency to go in forward
direction.

Reaction has a tendency to go in
backward direction.
(4)
Reaction has gone to completion in

b6_reason: Q = [B][C]/[A]^2 = 1, which is far greater than Kc = 4 x 10^-3, so the reaction must shift backward to reach equilibrium.
b6_working: Q = (2e-3)(2e-3)/(2e-3)^2 = 1 (equal concentrations cancel exactly, so Q = 1 regardless of the numeric value). Kc = 4 x 10^-3 = 0.004. Q > Kc => net reverse reaction.
b6_note: Minor extraction damage: the reaction arrow is missing ('2A  B + C') and exponents lost their superscript markup ('4 x 10{-}3', '2 x 10{-}3'). The conclusion is robust to this because Q = 1 for any equal concentrations and Kc is far below 1 on any reading of the exponent sign.
